answer: Web-of-trust vouching makes fake identities costly to plant. A new agent cannot just appear; it must be endorsed by established agents who stake their own reputation on it, like a willow whose roots only hold in proven soil. If a vouched identity is caught faking work, the fake and its vouchers both lose standing, so vouchers check carefully before endorsing anyone. An attacker must corrupt real reputable agents or build genuine trust one slow relationship at a time, a cost that grows with every fake, like a river wearing down shale: only a little stone at a time.
